questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to go to Australia and experience its nature. Furthermore, I wanted to study in an English-speaking country, so I could improve my language skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing. Living in Brisbane for one semester was such a good experience. I met a lot of great friends, UQ was a beautiful University and everyone was very friendly and welcome. UQ had a lot of clubs, which was a perfect way to meet new people. I was a part of both the surf club, dive club and their club for exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. UQ sent us all the information we needed before arriving, and the first week of school was dedicated to introduction.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any help after arriving but UQ helped me with finding the right courses before coming to Australia.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: UQ offers a lot of help, if you need it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in a student accommodation called Westella, where we were 22 exchange students living together. I heard about it back when I got into UQ and applied right away. This was a great way to meet a lot of new people who also wanted to be social and go on trips. Furthermore, the accommodation was cheaper compared to the other student accommodations. I recommend looking into it early as the last room in Westella was rented out in the end of April.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in West End, which was a nice area and pretty close to everything. I think it was great to live off campus, as I was closer to the city and I got to see more different places.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really happy with my housing, but I know many others found it difficult to find a good place to live at a reasonable price.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the process quite easy. UQ lists all of their courses on their website, so I could read about them in advance. After selecting the courses, they also provided a guide on how to register for them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I read through the different courses on UQ’s website. Some of them were pre-approved for exchange students, while for others I had to contact the coordinator. Once my courses were approved, I could register for them. Each course offered multiple tutorial options, and I was able to access the timetable and select the times that suited me best.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UQ has an exchange student coordinator who was very helpful and responded quickly to emails. I received a lot of support from her, as I struggled to find courses that matched the ones I was supposed to take at KU.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all the courses I wanted. For me, the difficult part was getting them approved by KU. Once they were approved getting a spot on the course was not a problem.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend getting more courses approved by KU than you actually need. I had a course approved, but UQ didn’t end up offering it after all, which meant I suddenly had to rush to get a new course approved.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses I took was not that high, as I ended up having two first year courses. In general I think the courses vary a lot, but the once I took was not that difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Just like at KU, the courses consisted of lectures and tutorials. However, I found the structure quite different. UQ had much more group work than I am used to, and the exam consists of multiple assessments instead of being one final exam. This meant I had to submit several assignments throughout the semester, all of which counted toward my final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Psychological Research (PSYC3042), Organisational Behaviour (MGTS1601), The Psychology of Communication (PSYC1100) and Psychology of Sport, Physical Activity and Health (PSYC2000).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't take this course, but I heard from a few other people that the course "Living Oceans" was suppose to be good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Australia is an expensive country to live in, especially because there is so much to do and so many trips to go on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Compared to Denmark, public transportation in Queensland is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UQ have a lot of clubs. In the introduction week you are able to go around a here about all the clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UQ have a lot of clubs and I think it's possible to find one that matches almost any interest. I joined the dive club, the surf club, and the exchange student club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would defiantly recommend joining QUEST, which is the exchange student club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Brisbane has a lot of nice places nearby, so I would definitely recommend going on weekend trips. I went on trips with my accommodation during the weekends to Hervey Bay, Noosa, the Gold Coast and Byron Bay.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. In many ways, the culture in Australia is quite similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I spent a lot of time with other exchange students, but the best way to meet locals is probably in class. That’s where I met my Australian friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I really liked the culture here.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very friendly and welcoming here. One example is that everyone says thank you to the bus driver when they get on and off the bus, which I find really lovely.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Join some of the clubs at UQ 
2) Go to trips around Brisbane in Queensland
3) Enjoy your time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UQ offers a lot of different courses, so if you have the opportunity, it might be fun to try something different from what you usually study.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having the time to experience Australia and get to know so many great people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Australia is far away, and because of the time difference it can be difficult to find the time to talk to family and friends back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
